title: PHORECAST: Enabling AI Understanding of Public Health Outreach Across Populations
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the ability of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to simulate and predict nuanced human responses (Likert scale opinions and free-form text) to public health messaging across diverse demographic subgroups. Specifically, religion was used as a key demographic factor to measure the models' predictive accuracy and the semantic text similarity between machine-generated responses and actual human responses across different religious affiliations.
findings: After fine-tuning on the PHORECAST dataset, models demonstrated improved accuracy and semantic similarity when emulating the responses of certain religious groups, most notably Muslims (response similarity for Islam increased by 0.12 for both models). However, disparities persisted and sometimes worsened for heavily underrepresented religious groups in the dataset, such as Agnostics and Hindus, where predictive accuracy decreased post-training (e.g., Gemma's accuracy for Agnostics dropped by 29.17%, and Llama's for Hindus dropped by 10.41%).
